items.text: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September and the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, the Labor Department reported.
items.detail: Nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000, well below economists' roughly 90,000 estimate. Private payrolls gained 46,000 while government employment fell 17,000. July was revised down by 31,000 to a loss of 10,000, and August down by 29,000 to a gain of 133,000 — 60,000 fewer jobs than previously reported for the two months combined. Average hourly earnings rose 3.0% over the year to $37.81. The labor force participation rate was 61.8%.
items.why: The main monthly jobs gauge came in soft a month before the midterms and ahead of the late-October Fed meeting.

items.text: CDC declared over a multistate Salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeño peppers that sickened 488 people in 34 states.
items.detail: As of Oct. 2, CDC said the Salmonella Javiana outbreak tied to fresh jalapeños from Sinaloa, Mexico, distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors is over. FDA closed its investigation the same day. Final counts: 488 illnesses, 65 hospitalizations and no deaths; illness onsets ran June 16 to Aug. 26. Traceback pointed to a common grower supplying Coast Citrus; recalled fresh jalapeños are past shelf life, though some longer-shelf products made with them remain on FDA's recall list.
items.why: Closes a nationwide foodborne outbreak that hit Chipotle, Qdoba and other Mexican-style restaurants.

items.text: A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, the UK Maritime Trade Operations office said.
items.detail: UKMTO said the master reported a hit at 1122 GMT during an outbound transit. The strike caused a small fire and a blackout; the fire was extinguished and the vessel continued underway. No casualties or environmental impact were reported. The incident follows Tuesday's strikes on three Liberian-flagged tankers in the same waterway.
items.why: Another confirmed kinetic hit on oil shipping through the strait that carries about a fifth of the world's oil.
items.source: UK Maritime Trade Operations / Anadolu Agency

items.text: Russian aerial attacks forced the partial closure of three Kyiv bridges over the Dnipro River, the capital's mayor said.
items.detail: Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said Russian strikes fully or partly closed three of Kyiv's six road bridges Friday, snarling traffic in what officials described as a new disruption tactic. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired more than 100 drones overnight, including jet-powered models, hitting Kyiv and eight other regions; a drone strike on a Kyiv high-rise killed one person. The European Commission said it disbursed €2.9 billion ($3.3 billion) in the latest financing batch to Ukraine.
items.why: Moscow shifted from energy and housing targets to choking the capital's river crossings.

upcoming.text: Supreme Court opens its new term and hears Suncor Energy v. Boulder County.
upcoming.detail: Whether federal law bars state-law lawsuits seeking damages from oil and gas companies for climate change. Justice Alito will not participate.
